statement: The Central and Eastern Europe Fund is a New York–listed closed-end fund run by DWS. It owns a portfolio of mostly Polish and Hungarian equities (banks, energy, insurers, retailers) plus a frozen Russian equity sleeve. Since 14 March 2022 the fund has carried those Russian holdings at zero under sanctions and capital controls, even though the share counts are still disclosed. The publicly reported net asset value therefore describes only the liquid book. The share price usually tracks that reported figure closely.

The interesting mispricing is not the thin discount to reported net asset value. It is that reported net asset value itself may understate economic ownership by writing the entire Russian book to zero. The predictive attribute is a Level-3 / sanctions zero mark: local Moscow prices still exist for many names, but a United States fund cannot freely realize them. If any path to recovery, private sale, or eventual unblocking opens, that sleeve is a free (or cheap) option on top of a solvent Central European equity portfolio. Buybacks when the fund trades below reported net asset value are a secondary catalyst, not the main edge.

Index and domestic yield buyers may underweight ASX royalty structures relative to US trust equivalents (MSB, SJT).

DaVita Inc. (NYSE: DVA) operates kidney dialysis centers and related lab services for patients with chronic kidney failure, primarily in the United States. **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$13.64 billion** and operating income was **$2.04 billion**. **[Fact]** FY2025 operating cash flow was **$1.89 billion** and capital spending was **$0.58 billion**, leaving **$1.31 billion** of normalized owner earnings. **[Fact]** The company reports a **single operating segment** (U.S. dialysis and related lab services). **[Inference]** DaVita is a scale-driven healthcare operator whose economics depend on treatment volumes, payer mix (Medicare, Medicare Advantage, commercial), and disciplined center-level cost control.

Evolve Royalties Ltd. is a Canadian junior royalty company listed on the CSE that collects cash from net profits interests and net smelter return royalties on copper, tin, and lithium projects without operating mines. **[Fact]** The portfolio spans 14 assets anchored by a 0.51% net profits interest on Teck's Highland Valley Copper mine, a 5% copper NSR on a portion of Hudbay's Copper Mountain mine, a sliding-scale tin gross-revenue royalty on Namibia's Uis mine, and a C$0.75 per tonne royalty on Eldorado Gold's McIlvenna Bay project (`EVR/presentations-and-media/corporate-presentation-2026-02.pdf`; `EVR/official-reports/news-release-2026-06-01-ytd-royalty-payments.txt`). **[Fact]** The company was formed by the Nomad Royalty team (sold to Sandstorm Gold for US$755 million in 2022) and listed on the CSE on December 17, 2025 after a reverse takeover with Voyageur Minerals Explorers Corp. **[Fact]** From January 1 through June 1, 2026, Evolve received C$2.70 million in royalty payments on roughly 55 million pro-forma shares outstanding.

statement: Fair Isaac sells a credit score and the software that uses scores in lending decisions. The three national credit bureaus, Experian, TransUnion, and Equifax, run the formula on their files and pay Fair Isaac a fee for each score. A smaller direct-to-consumer business sells scores at myFICO.com. The software segment covers fraud, origination, account management, and a subscription platform. In the year ended September 30, 2025, Scores were $1.17 billion and Software was $822 million.

statement: The September 29 selloff prices a break in mortgage score pricing power. That reading fits the last quarterly report, which said business-to-business score growth came mainly from a higher mortgage unit price. It does not fit a claim that the whole company just lost its customers. Classic FICO is still allowed at Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, and it is still required when a loan is underwritten by hand. The market can be wrong in either direction: too fearful if lenders keep paying up for the familiar score, or not fearful enough if the bureaus, who own the cheaper rival and distribute FICO, steer volume away.

There is no dated payoff or structural discount here. **[Inference]** Q1 2026 operating income **$1,665M** (+36% YoY vs **$1,221M**) reflects elevated transaction activity; the market may treat that run rate as permanent. **[Inference]** Our base return uses mid-cycle FY2025 free cash flow per share (**$7.41**), not the Q1 peak. Return is franchise earnings power at price, not a mispricing signal with a known catalyst date.

At **A$0.027** (Yahoo, ~4 Jun 2026), IDA still trades at roughly **56%** of Mar-2026 cash per share (~**A$0.0485**), not the extreme discount to Apr-2025 cash (~**A$0.11**) cited in the sponsor profile. The residual gap likely reflects **Loricatus litigation** (18% of net Tanzania proceeds preserved), **~A$0.9M/quarter legal spend**, exploration burn, and no maiden resource on Minos. The predictive attribute is **post-return cash floor plus legal resolution**: re-rating toward disclosed cash does not require a mine, but further distributions depend on dispute outcomes.

Terminal trust value on gas recovery uplift: **+$0.5/sh**

The market may treat San Juan as a broken income trust heading for wind-down, missing the Horizon Kinetics equity yield curve lens on a transitory NPI deficit. **[Inference]** Net excess production costs fell from **$6,328,902** at December 31, 2025 to **$4,640,115** at March 31, 2026, roughly **$1.69 million** recovered in one quarter, but Hilcorp's 2025 capex overspend slowed the path versus HK's May/June 2025 reinstatement estimate. **[Inference]** Royalty trusts sit outside yield screens and index mandates, creating a market-structure discount. If distributions resume, cumulative payoff may exceed what a zero-yield price embeds; timing and going-concern risk are worse than HK assumed.

Tesla designs, manufactures, and sells battery electric vehicles, energy storage systems, and solar products. **[Fact]** FY2025 consolidated revenue was approximately **$94.8 billion**, net income **$3.8 billion**, and operating cash flow **$14.7 billion** (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260129_rpt20251231_acc0001628280_26_003952.htm`). **[Fact]** Capital spending was **$8.5 billion**, implying free cash flow near **$6.2 billion** or about **$1.76 per diluted share** on **3.53 billion** weighted-average diluted shares. **[Fact]** Research and development expense was **$6.4 billion** in FY2025. **[Fact]** The company reports two operating segments: **Automotive** and **Energy Generation and Storage** (10-K segment note). **[Fact]** Q1 2026 revenue was **$22.4 billion** with net income **$477 million** (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-Q_20260423_rpt20260331_acc0001628280_26_026673.htm`).

The stock may price in robotaxi, Full Self-Driving subscription scale, or Optimus optionality that filings do not yet support as owner cash. **[Inference]** At roughly **$350** per share, the market may capitalize autonomy narratives while FY2025 diluted earnings per share was only **$1.08** and automotive margins face competition. **[Inference]** Energy storage is growing faster than auto but remains small relative to consolidated revenue; the market may overweight option value in the auto segment. **[Inference]** Heavy capital spending for AI training and new models may compress near-term free cash flow below the FY2025 normalized path.

New URC bolts **Sweetwater Royalties** (perpetual Wyoming Green River trona and soda ash royalties plus a large fee land estate) onto **Uranium Royalty Corp.** (uranium royalties, streams, and residual physical uranium). **[Fact]** Sweetwater's operators (WE Soda, Tata, Sisecam, Solvay/American Soda) have mined the basin for about 50 years; New URC owns **92%** of Sweetwater. **[Fact]** URC brings uranium deal skills and a mostly pre-cash royalty book; legacy shareholders own about **41%** of the combined company after the arrangement closed **2026-07-27**. **[Fact]** The public parent moved to Delaware and listed on NASDAQ **2026-07-28**, exiting the Canadian PFIC profile for *new* U.S. holders after domestication.

statement: Starting free cash flow per share: **$0.05**

The market may still price this as a sleepy foreign uranium royalty name, or as a soda-ash story at the wrong point in the cycle. **[Inference]** The real security is a **levered scarce-land royalty stub**: cash today is weak because soda ash is in a deep downturn, but the mineral estate is long-duration and capital-light for the owner. **[Inference]** Mispricing can also come from **deal optics** (deemed **US$3.64**) versus **equity math after US$625m debt**. **[Fact]** Pro forma FY2025 Sweetwater royalty revenue fell to **US$59.3m** from **US$82.5m** prior year (circular pro formas), consistent with generational soda-ash oversupply commentary from basin operators. Predictive attribute: **market_structure_discount** (complex deal, leverage, PFIC history, and uranium label on a trona-heavy cash engine).
